### Wednesday (9/30) [...] That's a tough lead-up to management's report on fiscal 2027 first-quarter results after the closing bell on Thursday. Wall Street expects a 10.2% year-over-year slide for EPS to 44 cents, on a 3.3% decline for revenue.

The consumer discretionary stock was down almost 42% year to date and more than 77% from its November 5, 2021, all-time high through September 24. Its market cap has fallen from a peak of about $281 billion to $53.5 billion.

Headline PCE was up 0.3% month over month vs 0.1% in July and a Wall Street estimate of 0.4%.

Core PCE, which removes volatile food and energy prices from the equation, was up 3.0% year over year and 0.2% month over month.

"Although these lower inflation readings are encouraging," observes Raymond James Chief Economist Eugenio J. Alemán, "it is unlikely to change the current view of Federal Reserve officials regarding interest rates going forward."
